findings.F1: Sense 1 example states the melting point of iron, a checkable science fact.
findings.F2: The pronunciation fact is duplicated in pronunciation.notes and in the pronunciation adaptation note.
findings.F3: iron-v appears in both word_family and see_also.
findings.F4: The definition of 'strike while the iron is hot' says the opposite of the idiom's meaning (act quickly while the chance is good).
findings.F5: Missing coverage of iron as a mineral in food and the body.
findings.F6: The grammar adaptation note only restates the sense countability values.
findings.F7: Wrong American IPA ˈɪ.rɑn; it should be ˈaɪ.ɚn.
